initialize.instructions:
This server provides tools for interacting with Unison Code locally, such as typechecking or reading
        documentation, as well as tools for searching Unison Share, which is a platform for sharing Unison projects and
        libraries.

        It also provides some mechanisms for editing and updating local Unison projects, such as installing libraries
        from Unison Share.

        Before doing any work in unison please read the file://unison-guide resource for information on how to write
        Unison.

tools.description: Search Unison Share for projects and libraries.

query.description: The search query to use. E.g. "http client". By default, each search word is ANDed together, but you can use OR to search for multiple terms. E.g. "http OR client" will return results that match either term. You can also exclude results using "-", e.g. "-http" will exclude results that match the term "http". Wrap a term in quotes to search for an exact phrase, e.g. ""http client"" will search for the exact phrase "http client".

tools.description:
Typecheck a code snippet within the context of a project. Only definitions which which are part of libraries or which have been previously added or updated will be available to reference within code.

          The result will indicate any errors and suggested fixes, or will indicate that the code typechecks and is ready to add or update.

          If you would like to test the behaviour of any pure functions, you may prefix a code snippet with an angle bracket.

          e.g.

          ```
          > 1 + 2
          ```

          Or

          ```
          > let
              isGreaterThan3 x = x > 3
              isGreaterThan3 4
          ```

          If you wish to write unit tests, you may do so like this:

          ```
          test> Nat.tests.additionIsCommutative = test.verify do
            Each.repeat 100
            n = Random.natIn 0 1000
            m = Random.natIn 0 1000
            ensureEqual (n + m) (m + n)
          ```

          If you intend to update code, you may call the Update Definitions tool directly instead, it will typecheck and update in one step.

code.description: The source code to typecheck. Either the `sourceCode` key or the `filePath`, but not both.

filePath.description: The absolute file path to the source code to typecheck.

branchName.description: The branch of the project to work within, e.g. `main` or `develop`

projectName.description: The name of the project to work within, e.g. `@unison/base` or `@ceedubs/json`

tools.description: Delete one or more definitions (terms or types) from the codebase.

force.description: If true, force delete even if the definition has dependents. Default is false.

names.description: The names of the definitions to delete.

items.description: A definition name to delete, e.g. `mynamespace.foo` or `MyType`.

branchName.description: The branch of the project to work within, e.g. `main` or `develop`

projectName.description: The name of the project to work within, e.g. `@unison/base` or `@ceedubs/json`

tools.name: delete-definitions

tools.description: Rename a definition (term, type, or namespace) by changing only its final name segment. The parent path is preserved. For example, `rename foo.bar.baz Qux` changes the name `baz` to `Qux`, producing `foo.bar.Qux`. To move a definition to a different namespace, use `move-to` instead.

newNameSegment.description: The new name segment (final part only). For example, to rename `foo.bar` to `foo.baz`, provide `baz`. The parent path is preserved.

oldName.description: The current name of the definition to rename, e.g. `mynamespace.foo` or `MyType`.

branchName.description: The branch of the project to work within, e.g. `main` or `develop`

projectName.description: The name of the project to work within, e.g. `@unison/base` or `@ceedubs/json`

tools.name: rename-definition

tools.description: Move a definition (term, type, or namespace) to a completely new path. For example, `move foo.bar baz.qux` renames `foo.bar` to `baz.qux`. This changes the full path, not just the final segment.

newName.description: The new full path for the definition, e.g. `othernamespace.bar` or `NewType`. Can move to a different namespace.

oldName.description: The current full path of the definition to move, e.g. `mynamespace.foo` or `MyType`.

branchName.description: The branch of the project to work within, e.g. `main` or `develop`

projectName.description: The name of the project to work within, e.g. `@unison/base` or `@ceedubs/json`

tools.name: move-definition

tools.description: Move one or more definitions or namespaces into a destination namespace. The final segment of each source is preserved. For example, `moveTo foo.bar dest` moves `foo.bar` into namespace `dest`, producing `dest.bar`. Multiple sources can be moved at once: `moveTo foo bar baz dest` moves all three into `dest`.

destination.description: The destination namespace to move the sources into, e.g. `othernamespace` or `foo.bar`. Each source's final segment is preserved.

branchName.description: The branch of the project to work within, e.g. `main` or `develop`

projectName.description: The name of the project to work within, e.g. `@unison/base` or `@ceedubs/json`

sources.description: The paths of the definitions or namespaces to move. The final segment of each source is preserved in the destination.

items.description: A path to move, e.g. `mynamespace.foo` or `MyType`.

tools.name: move-to

tools.description: Delete a namespace and all definitions within it from the codebase.

force.description: If true, force delete even if definitions in the namespace have dependents. Default is false.

namespaceName.description: The name of the namespace to delete, e.g. `mynamespace` or `foo.bar`. This will delete the namespace and all definitions within it.

branchName.description: The branch of the project to work within, e.g. `main` or `develop`

projectName.description: The name of the project to work within, e.g. `@unison/base` or `@ceedubs/json`

tools.name: delete-namespace

tools.description: Get the reflog (history of branch state changes) for a project or branch. Returns structured data about recent changes.

includeTimestamps.description: Whether to include timestamps in the output. Default is true.

limit.description: Maximum number of entries to return. Default is 100.

branchName.description: The branch of the project to work within, e.g. `main` or `develop`

projectName.description: The name of the project to work within, e.g. `@unison/base` or `@ceedubs/json`

scope.description: The scope of the reflog: 'branch' (default) shows entries for the current branch, 'project' shows entries for all branches in the project, 'global' shows entries for all projects.

tools.name: reflog

tools.description: Get the causal history of a branch, showing changes over time. Returns structured data about commits and diffs.

diffLimit.description: Maximum number of diff elements to show per entry. Default is 10.

limit.description: Maximum number of history entries to return. Default is 100.

branchName.description: The branch of the project to work within, e.g. `main` or `develop`

projectName.description: The name of the project to work within, e.g. `@unison/base` or `@ceedubs/json`

startHash.description: Optional causal hash to start history from. If not provided, starts from the current branch head.

tools.name: history

tools.description: Create a new branch in a project. Can create from the current context, as an empty branch, or from an existing branch.

newBranchName.description: The name for the new branch, e.g. `feature/my-feature` or `develop`

projectName.description: The name of the project to create the branch in, e.g. `@unison/base` or `@ceedubs/json`

sourceBranchName.description: When sourceType is 'branch', the name of the source branch to copy from.

sourceBranchProject.description: When sourceType is 'branch', the project containing the source branch. Optional - defaults to the target project if not specified.

sourceType.description: The source for the new branch: 'current' creates from current context, 'empty' creates an empty branch, 'branch' creates from an existing branch specified by sourceBranchProject and sourceBranchName

tools.name: create-branch
